reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown limit 'all his house' to the kin and courtiers present at Gilboa, since Chronicles elsewhere names sons who clearly survived.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats Chronicles' seamless Saul-to-David succession as a deliberate reshaping of Samuel's fuller narrative, of which this 'all his house died' claim is one instance.

quotes.text: We have before us a deliberate and in its motives a very transparent mutilation of the original narrative as preserved for us in the Book of Samuel.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Chronicler's suppression of the Saulide succession narrative found in Samuel.

sides.snippet: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Yahweh's oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
sides.verseText: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of Yahweh's oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

sides.snippet: So Saul died, and his three sons; and all his house died together.
sides.verseText: So Saul died, and his three sons; and all his house died together.
